inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average FY2026 (2,224m shares in issue excluding own shares + 7m dilutive potential ordinary shares; FY2026 AR line 10344). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and no buyback is running (programme paused since FY2024 to de-lever), so the flat count is a modelling convention the company is funding with cash dividends rather than repurchases.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company net borrowings $20,482m (FY2026 AR note 17, line 13283) less lease liabilities $685m = $19,797m. total_debt = gross borrowings $22,002m less leases $685m = $21,317m, i.e. bonds and loans $21,511m plus the net fair value of the cross-currency/interest-rate hedges (-$194m) that manage them. Leases excluded under lease treatment (B) below. Post-employment benefit deficit ($387m pre-tax) is deducted in the equity bridge, net of tax.
inputs.sbc_source: DGE.L_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2026 $44m (share-based payment expense, FY2026 annual report). Equity-award cash taxes nil (EquityAwardTaxes kpi 0 every year). Interest income ($292m received) NOT stripped: Diageo carries $19.8bn net debt, there is no net-cash pile to double count. Note reported_fcf (OCF $4,392m less capex $1,197m) is the company's post-interest definition ($752m net interest paid inside OCF); the forward flows are built unlevered from components and net borrowings are deducted in the bridge, so last_fcf is an anchor, not the year-1 flow.
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in USD (Diageo redenominated from GBP to USD from FY2024; FY2019-FY2023 rows of the Metrics CSV are GBP, flagged per row in the Currency column). LSE quote in GBp (pence). fx_rate converts model USD per ordinary share to GBp: 100 / GBPUSD 1.3233 = 75.569 (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-10-09). Parity check against the NYSE ADR: DEO $86.73 (2026-10-09 close) / 4 ordinary shares per ADS = $21.68 x 75.569 = 1,638.5p vs observed DGE.L 1,638.0p, a 0.03% tie that confirms rate, direction and the 4:1 ADS ratio.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the flows' currency: risk-free 4.1% (US 10y, Oct-2026), equity beta 0.85 for a global spirits staple, ERP 5.0% gives cost of equity ~8.4%; after-tax cost of debt ~3.0% (effective interest rate 3.9% per FY2026 AR line 1293, 24% tax); market cap ~$48bn vs net debt $19.8bn gives D/V ~29%. Mechanical WACC ~6.8%; rounded to 7.0% and held identical across all three scenarios -- turnaround, tariff and leverage risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. Lease cash (ROU depreciation $151m, FY2026 AR line 12245, plus ~$30m lease interest on $685m of liabilities at ~4.5%) is charged inside EBIT as lease_cost_pct_path 0.8% of revenue; lease liabilities excluded from net debt; D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex-ROU ($749m company D&A less $151m ROU = ~$600m, 3.0% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. NCI profit $221m FY2026 (USL 44% minority, Shui Jing Fang, Ketel One JV, EABL 35% until disposal) is ~4.3% of pre-exceptional pre-tax profit; ex-EABL ~3.5%. Folded into cash_tax_rate_path as leakage (24.3% pre-exceptional tax rate + ~3.5% NCI = ~28%). NCI equity ($2,083m book) is NOT deducted in the bridge.
inputs.associates_treatment: EBITDA in the flows is ex-associates: company adjusted EBITDA $6,650m (FY2026 AR line 13234) less $218m share of associates = $6,432m, 32.7% of net sales. The matching asset -- investments in associates and JVs, principally the 34% Moet Hennessy stake -- is added to the bridge at its $5,284m carrying value (AR line 10422). MH dividends received ($116m) are therefore also excluded from the flows.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (capex/D&A normalising and margin recovering through the Accelerate programme, so the year-5 margin is not yet mature). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md as a non-US consumer operating company with the adaptations file applied (currency, leases, NCI, matching assets). Fresh build -- no prior DCF for DGE.L (the DEO ADR was valued separately on 2026-10-03 on a per-ADS basis). FY0 = FY2026 (year to 30 June 2026): net sales $19,643m (-3.0% reported, -2.0% organic), operating profit pre-exceptionals $5,683m, exceptional operating charges $2,527m (impairments $1,489m Turkiye/Don Papa, restructuring $908m), reported operating margin 16.1% vs organic 29.4%. EABL: 65% stake agreed for sale to Asahi (Dec-2025), estimated net proceeds $2.3bn after tax, implied EV $4.8bn, 17x EBITDA, completion H2 CY2026. Modelled as sold: EABL (~$1.0bn net sales, ~5% of group) is stripped from the flows through a -5pt year-1 growth hit and the $2.3bn proceeds sit in the equity bridge. The RCB cricket team sale by USL is not in the bridge (proceeds accrue 44% to USL minorities; treated as leverage upside only). Working capital: a spirits maker with ~$8.5bn maturing inventory and receivables well above payables consumes cash on growth, so wc_capture_pct is negative (-20%); year-1 revenue decline from the EABL deconsolidation therefore books a ~$180m WC release that is an artefact (~0.3% of equity value), accepted and disclosed. Guidance (FY2026 AR lines 1237-1250): FY27 broadly flat organic net sales, low-to-mid single digit organic operating profit growth, FCF c.$2bn after c.$750m exceptional cash; FY27-29 LSD organic net sales CAGR, MSD organic operating profit CAGR, cumulative FCF c.$8bn after c.$850m exceptional cash, leverage ~2.75x FY27 and c.2x by end FY29. Base case lands slightly below that guidance (unlevered owner FCF ~$3.3-3.6bn vs ~$3.7bn implied); bull matches it.

equity_bridge.item: EABL disposal net proceeds (65% stake to Asahi, after tax and costs)
equity_bridge.note: H2 FY2026 results presentation line 798; EABL stripped from flows via year-1 growth

equity_bridge.note: c.$850m pre-tax (AR line 1249) x (1 - 24%), lightly discounted; not in the component flows

historical_growth.basis_note: FY2019-FY2023 statements are GBP, FY2024 onward USD. CAGRs below convert the GBP start year at the approximate average GBP/USD of that year (FY2021 1.38, FY2023 1.21) for trend context only; the cash-flow base is the USD FY2026 actual.
historical_growth.eps_note: Reported EPS per ordinary share, 78.1c FY2026 vs 164.9p FY2023 and 113.8p FY2021, collapsed by $2.5bn FY2026 and $1.4bn FY2025 exceptional charges. Pre-exceptional EPS was 165.3c FY2026, +0.7% on FY2025 and roughly -2%/yr on FY2021 in USD.
historical_growth.fcf_note: Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not stripped, net-debt company): $3,151m FY2026 vs GBP1,795m FY2023 (~$2.17bn, a destocking trough with -GBP768m working capital) and GBP2,979m FY2021 (~$4.11bn, pandemic-recovery peak). The 5yr owner-FCF CAGR (-5.2%) is below the reported-FCF CAGR by ~0.1pt only: SBC is immaterial at 0.2% of revenue, so none of the history is paid for in stock.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management FY27-29 low-single-digit organic net sales ambition, cross-checked against the 5yr equity CAGR (2.7%) and 5yr revenue CAGR (2.2%); base-case path averages ~2% over 10 years after the EABL deconsolidation.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs (-13%/-27%) diverge far more than 30% from equity (+2.7%/+4.7%) and revenue (+2.2%/-1.7%). Cause is exceptional impairments and restructuring, not the operating trend (organic operating profit +2.0% FY2026). Growth selected from the organic trend and guidance, not from EPS.

base.growth_note: FY27: organic flat (guidance) less EABL deconsolidation (-5pt) plus ~0.5pt FX tailwind. FY28-29 LSD organic per guidance, FY30-32 3% as US spirits normalises and India/LAC/Guinness compound, fading to 2.5% terminal.
base.ebitda_margin_note: FY2026 actual 32.7% ex-associates (organic operating margin 29.4% + 3.8% D&A, minus lease). FY27 dips 20bps on tariffs (~$100m net after mitigation) and the loss of EABL's beer margin; then ~30bps/yr from the c.$1bn operating-framework/supply savings, about a third dropping through after reinvestment in marketing. Peaks at 34%, 1.6pt below the FY2022 35%+ level -- deliberately not recovered.
base.capex_note: FY2026 6.1% ($1,197m) after 8.0% FY2025 and 7.4% FY2024. Guided FY27-29 cumulative capex $3.75bn (~$1.25bn/yr, ~6.5% of ex-EABL revenue; Analysis.json guidance block) for Guinness capacity and supply agility; tapers to 5% from FY32 as projects commission, while D&A ex-ROU rises from 3.0% toward 4.0%. Capex stays above D&A throughout (maturing-stock business).
base.cash_tax_note: 24.3% pre-exceptional tax rate (AR line 1298; cash taxes paid were $817m FY2026, $1,114m FY2025) plus ~3.5% NCI leakage ex-EABL. FY27 1pt lower on restructuring deductions.
base.narrative: Organic turnaround executes to the lower end of guidance.

bull.narrative: US spirits destocking ends in FY27, tequila and Guinness resume share gains, Accelerate savings drop through; margins recover to the FY2022 level by FY31.

bear.narrative: Structural moderation plus tariffs: US spirits volumes keep falling, USMCA tequila exemption lost, savings reinvested just to hold share; margins settle at 30%.

scenario_narratives.base: The organic turnaround under Sir Dave Lewis executes at the lower end of guidance. FY27 organic net sales are flat (US spirits still down low-single-digit, Europe/LAC/India growing), reported revenue falls ~4.5% as EABL deconsolidates. From FY28 organic growth returns to 2-3% as US wholesaler destocking is lapped, Don Julio and Guinness keep growing and India and Africa compound. The c.$1bn operating-framework and supply savings land, with roughly a third dropping to margin and the rest reinvested in marketing (reinvestment rate back toward 17-18% from 16.2%); EBITDA margin ex-associates recovers from 32.7% to 34% by FY32 but does not regain the FY2022 peak. Tariffs stay at 10% UK / 15% EU with Mexico/Canada exempt under USMCA, a ~$100m net drag after mitigation. Capex normalises from 6% to 5% of revenue as Guinness and agave capacity commissions. Leverage falls to ~2x by FY29 via EABL proceeds and the 30-50% payout policy; the buyback does not restart inside the explicit horizon.
scenario_narratives.bull: US spirits returns to growth in FY27 as the two-year destock and the GLP-1/moderation narrative prove cyclical rather than structural; tequila (Don Julio, Casamigos RTS) and Guinness take share and the RTD portfolio scales. Lewis's savings over-deliver as Accelerate did ($540m secured vs guidance) and more of the c.$1bn drops through, taking EBITDA margin ex-associates to 35.5% by FY33, i.e. the FY2022 level. Organic growth runs 3.5-4.5% through FY30 (India, LAC, Africa ex-EABL, Chinese white spirits recovering from the CWS trough) and the RCB and further non-core disposals accelerate de-leveraging, allowing buybacks to resume by FY29 (not modelled -- flat count). Terminal 3%, 20x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: Moderation is structural: US spirits volumes decline 2-3% a year for the rest of the decade, premiumisation reverses as consumers trade down, and the USMCA exemption on Mexican spirits is lost so tequila -- Diageo's largest growth engine -- carries a tariff on top. Turkiye hyperinflation and CWS keep impairing; a new CEO's cost savings are consumed defending share and the reinvestment rate has to rise. EBITDA margin ex-associates drifts to 30% and stays there, organic growth is ~1.5% nominal, leverage stays near 3x so the dividend is held at the 50c floor. Terminal growth 1.5%, 15x cap. Not a solvency case -- the A-band balance sheet, $5bn of associates and disposable non-core assets rule that out -- but a permanently lower-multiple, ex-growth staple.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house 15/50/35 to 25/50/25, matching the DEO ADR valuation of 2026-10-03. Bear raised because three independent risks are live at once: a first-year CEO turnaround whose savings are not yet in the P&L, US tariff policy on which the tequila franchise depends (USMCA exemption is a political variable), and 3.1x leverage above the company's own 2.5-3.0x range. Bull cut because it needs the US consumer, tariff status quo and savings drop-through all to go right simultaneously.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Diageo is valued as a mature, high-margin spirits compounder in the trough of a three-year US destocking cycle, on unlevered owner FCF built from a 32.7% ex-associates EBITDA margin that is allowed to recover only part-way to its FY2022 peak. The valuation deliberately does not extrapolate FY2022 margins, does not credit the full c.$1bn savings programme, and charges the EABL disposal, the Moet Hennessy stake, the pension deficit and the guided restructuring cash explicitly in the bridge rather than inside the flows. Risk is charged in the flows and the 25% bear weight, not in the 7% USD WACC. House and street bases nearly coincide because SBC is 0.2% of revenue.
key_risks_to_valuation: US spirits demand: whether the post-2023 decline is destocking (cyclical) or GLP-1/moderation (structural) is the single largest swing between bull and bear
Tariffs: loss of the USMCA exemption on Mexican spirits would hit Don Julio and Casamigos directly; the current 10% UK / 15% EU tariffs cost ~$200m pre-mitigation
Leverage: 3.1x net debt/EBITDA with the dividend cut to a 30-50% payout; EABL completion ($2.3bn, assumed in the bridge) is subject to regulatory approval
Turnaround execution: new CEO, new operating framework, S/4HANA migration and $908m restructuring charge all landing in the same year
Emerging-market translation and hyperinflation (Turkiye, Nigeria, Argentina) and Chinese white spirits (Shui Jing Fang) impairment risk
Associates: Moet Hennessy carried at $5.3bn is exposed to the cognac/champagne downturn and LVMH's call option over the stake
Currency: USD flows against a GBp quote; a 10% move in GBP/USD moves the pence value by 10% with no change in the business

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular LSE close); 52-week range 1,295.5p-1,903.9p. GBP/USD from Yahoo GBPUSD=X on the same date; DEO ADR close used as the parity check.
data_sources.financials: DGE.L_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, FY2018-FY2026 plus H1 FY2025/H1 FY2026); FY2026 annual report (DGE.L_Annual_FY2026.txt) for adjusted EBITDA, net borrowings, leases, associates, NCI, diluted shares and guidance; H2 FY2026 results presentation for EABL deal terms and tariff exposure.
data_sources.qualitative: DGE.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10) read after the first build: its bull/bear axes match the scenario narratives; its guidance block (FY27-29 capex $3.75bn, RoW 3-5% growth, North America share stabilisation from year two) lifted the FY27-29 capex path. FY2026 annual report strategy, outlook and risk sections and the H2 FY2026 results presentation for the rest.
